Identify geometry and magnetic properties of each complex:
- [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺: high-spin d⁶, 4 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic, octahedral.
- [Ni(CO)₄]: tetrahedral (4 ligands), Ni(0) d¹⁰ diamagnetic but geometry not octahedral.
- [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺: high-spin d⁶, 4 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic, octahedral.
- [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻: low-spin d⁶ (t₂g⁶), all electrons paired → diamagnetic, octahedral.
- [Co(CN)₆]³⁻: low-spin d⁶ (t₂g⁶), all electrons paired → diamagnetic, octahedral.
- [MnCl₄]²⁻: typically tetrahedral (or possibly square planar), high-spin d⁵ → paramagnetic, not octahedral.
- [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: low-spin d⁶ (t₂g⁶), all electrons paired → diamagnetic, octahedral.
- [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺: likely tetrahedral (4 ligands) or square planar; Zn²⁺ d¹⁰ diamagnetic but geometry not octahedral (only 4 ligands given).

Thus the species that are both diamagnetic and have octahedral geometry are: [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Co(CN)₆]³⁻, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺. That gives 3 species.

Answer: 3.

5. [Co(CN)₆]³⁻: octahedral, Co³⁺ d⁶, strong field → low spin → diamagnetic ✓.
6. [MnCl₄]²⁻: tetrahedral, Mn²⁺ d⁵ high spin → paramagnetic.
7. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: octahedral, Co³⁺ d⁶, low spin → diamagnetic ✓.
8. [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺: tetrahedral, d¹⁰ diamagnetic but not octahedral.
